While formulating these geographic expansion and penetration strategies, it is essential to acknowledge the evolution and limitations of available market intelligence. Expectations are heavily weighted toward minimal turnaround times, transparent pricing models, and the use of high-quality replacement parts. Furthermore, as the logistics industry becomes more integrated and complex, fleet operators increasingly look for service providers who can offer comprehensive, end-to-end solutions rather than fragmented repairs. Fleet managers expect their service partners to act as extensions of their own operations, proactively identifying potential system failures before they result in costly on-road breakdowns. Cost management remains the foremost challenge and operational focus for government fleet administrators, who must constantly balance the necessity of fleet readiness against stringent budget constraints. Over half of fleet managers cite rising operational expenses as their primary concern in the current economic climate [54] . This financial pressure is exacerbated by volatile fuel prices, extended delivery lead times for new vehicles, and escalating acquisition costs, which collectively compel government agencies to adopt forward-looking strategies such as lifecycle extension and proactive maintenance [51][53] . To optimize maintenance expenditures, public sector fleets are increasingly exploring alternative service models. For instance, recent directives have advised state agencies to rely on Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) garages for routine maintenance and repair services, a move designed to leverage localized expertise while controlling labor costs [55] . These financial strategies underscore the critical need for cost-effective maintenance partnerships that can deliver reliable service without exceeding rigid public sector budgets. The adoption of emerging technologies is viewed as an essential mechanism for improving maintenance efficiency and mitigating the impacts of rising operational costs.
